title: When the Hollow Falls
premise: Freya Hartwell, a mercenary whose war-god Vaskar fell silent fifteen years ago, has survived as a charm-seller in Corvale, a city where the Magistrate's Wardens burn magic-users at the Hollow Falls. When prayers to the old gods suddenly start being answered, Freya discovers her god's silence was a wound inflicted by the Wardens' founders, and that every answered prayer is tearing open the seal that keeps Vaskar's vengeful twin bound beneath the Falls. Hunted by a Warden captain who was once her sworn sister, Freya must choose between exposing the truth that would free the persecuted faithful and keeping a secret that damns them all. In the end she breaks the seal herself, sacrificing her connection to Vaskar to bind the twin with her own sworn oath, and the survivors build a fragile new covenant between gods and mortals that no law can outlaw.
about_author: Jude Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-formulae and heretical pamphlets before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about broken covenants and the people stubborn enough to keep their word anyway.

chapters.title: The Quiet God
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In Corvale's night market, Freya sells a luck-charm to a desperate mother, then privately performs a fifteen-year-dead ritual to Vaskar and gets no answer, as always. Emotional beat: the ache of loyal service to a god who may not exist, establishing her careful, invisible life.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A Warden raid torches the neighboring stall of a hedge-witch Freya secretly supplies. Watching the woman dragged toward the Falls, Freya does nothing, and hates herself for it. Emotional beat: guilt and the cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: An Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A beggar child's prayer at a wayside shrine is audibly answered, and the shrine-stone warms in Freya's hand, humming with Vaskar's old battle-cadence. The gods are waking. Emotional beat: terror and wild, unwelcome hope.

chapters.title: The Warden's Face
chapters.summary: Captain Sera Voss's POV. Sera, Freya's former oath-sister from the mercenary company, now leads the Wardens, interrogates the captured hedge-witch and finds a sigil matching Freya's old company mark. Emotional beat: duty hardening over old love.

chapters.title: What the Seal Remembers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Following the hum beneath the city, Freya reaches the Hollow Falls and hears two voices in the water: Vaskar, faint and wounded, and something hungrier beneath him. She learns the Wardens' founders wounded Vaskar to forge a seal. Emotional beat: revelation that rewrites her fifteen years of abandonment.

chapters.title: Company of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya seeks the last living member of her old company, the one-eyed quartermaster Bram, who confirms the truth and gives her Vaskar's stolen heartstone, entrusted to their company long ago. Emotional beat: reluctant re-entry into a war she thought was over.

chapters.title: Sera's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera burns the company roster to protect old comrades but cannot bring herself to strike Freya's name, even as her superiors order the 'Hartwell woman' found. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in Sera's loyalty to the law.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's War
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya begins passing real, working charms to the persecuted faithful of the undercity, becoming the answer to prayers she never meant to answer. Emotional beat: purpose rekindling, and the danger of becoming visible.

chapters.title: Blood in the Shrine-Water
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. A raid on an undercity chapel goes wrong when the awakened god's power flares; three Wardens die, and Sera finds Freya's charm-work among the wreckage. Emotional beat: betrayal felt personally, the hunt becoming intimate.

chapters.title: The Hollow Beneath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the Falls, the bound twin, Hollow-Vaskar, speaks to Freya through the heartstone, offering her everything her silent god never gave: answers, power, acknowledgment. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by fifteen years of neglect.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Oaths
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram tells the full history: the company's founders swore the original binding with a living oath, and only a sworn heart can renew or break it. He warns Freya that Sera will not be able to choose her. Emotional beat: dread and inheritance.

chapters.title: The Trap at Tanner's Row
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Using a child informant, Sera corners Freya in the undercity; they fight, and Freya refuses to strike a killing blow, instead showing Sera the heartstone's truth. Emotional beat: the past surging up between drawn blades.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Shaken, Sera reads the sealed founding archives and learns the Wardens' justice was built on a lie and a stolen god. She burns her report. Emotional beat: faith in the law collapsing.

chapters.title: The Silence Explained
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Vaskar, faint but present, finally answers: he has been conscious all fifteen years, sealed alongside his twin, unable to speak, his silence the price of the binding holding. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into fury at everyone who let her believe she was forsaken.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The Magistrate, aware the seal is weakening, plans to feed a mass execution of the faithful to the Falls to strengthen it. Sera is ordered to herd the prisoners. Emotional beat: complicity demanded, conscience refusing.

chapters.title: Sisters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Sera comes to Freya not with warrants but with the execution roster; old oaths are re-sworn, this time in truth rather than habit. Emotional beat: reconciliation hard-won and unsentimental.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Falls
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Freya and Sera prepare a desperate plan to break the prisoners out and reach the seal before the Magistrate's rite; Bram gathers the last of the old company. Emotional beat: quiet courage, the calm before catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Rite at the Falls
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The escape collapses; the Magistrate begins the execution, and the blood feeds Hollow-Vaskar, who begins tearing free. Vaskar's voice and the twin's roar shake the city. Emotional beat: everything failing at once.

chapters.title: The Choice of Oaths
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the brink of the Falls, Freya understands: the seal requires a sworn heart freely given. She offers her fifteen-year oath, her bond to Vaskar, her name in the god's mouth, to bind the twin anew. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: What Freya Hartwell Paid
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The binding takes; the twin is sealed, but Freya collapses, deaf now to all gods, her magic gone. Sera holds the Magistrate's forces at bay with the truth read aloud to the crowd. Emotional beat: victory that feels like a funeral.

chapters.title: A City Without Warden Law
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The Magistrate falls; Sera refuses the captaincy and instead founds a covenant-court where the faithful and faithless are judged alike, with the freed prisoners as its first witnesses. Emotional beat: justice rebuilt outside the law that failed.

chapters.title: The Unanswered Prayer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Months later, Freya sells honest charms in the night market, magic now lawful but her own gift silent. A child prays at the rebuilt shrine, and though no god answers, Freya does, with her own two hands. Emotional beat: belonging found not in a god's voice but in human choice, quiet and hard-won.
